title: Order by Name
description: Write a query to get all students sorted by name alphabetically.
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY name;
explanation: ORDER BY sorts results. Without DESC, sorting is ascending by default.

title: Order by Age Descending
description: Write a query to get all students sorted by age from oldest to youngest.
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY age DESC;
explanation: DESC keyword sorts in descending order (highest to lowest).

title: Limit Results
description: Write a query to get the first 2 students from the students table.
explanation: LIMIT restricts the number of rows returned by the query.

title: ORDER BY Syntax
description: Which clause is used to sort query results?
hints: It comes after FROM and WHERE
explanation: ORDER BY is the clause used to sort result sets.

title: Sort by Multiple Columns
description: Write a query to get students sorted by grade first, then by age descending within each grade.
hints: List multiple columns in ORDER BY
Apply DESC to the last column
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY grade, age DESC;
explanation: Multiple columns are sorted in the order listed. Secondary sorting applies within groups of the first column.

title: Top 3 Courses
description: Write a query to get the 3 courses with the highest credit hours.
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM courses ORDER BY credits DESC LIMIT 3;
explanation: Combining ORDER BY with LIMIT gives you the top N records.

title: Fix Sort Order
description: This query should return students sorted by age ascending, but it's wrong. Fix it: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY age DESC;
solutionSql: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY age ASC;
explanation: ASC means ascending order (lowest to highest). It's the default, so you can omit it.
brokenQuery: SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY age DESC;

title: Predict Sorted Output
description: What will this query return? SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name LIMIT 2;
explanation: Names sorted alphabetically: Alice, Bob, Charlie, Diana, Eve. First 2 are Alice and Bob.
